verifications.title: Emoji in item names (e.g., `🍔 Big Burger`)
verifications.evidence: No current seeded item contains emoji (verified DB). Rendering paths: (1) Vue mustache → browsers render emoji natively. (2) POS Vanilla wizard `innerHTML +=` → browsers render emoji natively. (3) Browser print to thermal printer via window.print() → OS print spooler converts (often successful on macOS, mixed on Linux CUPS). (4) ESC/POS direct path → `encodeForPrinter()` would call `iconv('UTF-8', 'CP858//TRANSLIT//IGNORE', '🍔')` which strips the multibyte emoji silently (TRANSLIT has no Latin1 mapping for emoji); final fallback `preg_replace('/[^\\x20-\\x7E\\x0A\\x0D]/', '?', $text)` would render `?`. JSON serialization: PHP `json_encode` with default flags stores emoji as UTF-16 surrogate pair `\ud83c\udf54` for `🍔`; with `JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE` stores raw 4-byte UTF-8.
verifications.graceful_degradation: Browser-driven receipt (current architecture): emoji renders if printer driver supports it; otherwise printer driver renders fallback glyph. ESC/POS direct (dead path): emoji deterministically becomes `?`. JSON storage: round-trips correctly via json_decode.

verifications.title: URL encoding in Idempotency-Key
verifications.evidence: `IdempotencyKeyMiddleware::handle` L61: `if (! preg_match('/^[A-Za-z0-9._\\-]{8,64}$/', $key))` → throws `MissingIdempotencyKeyException` ('8-64 chars ASCII') for any header containing `+`, `%`, `=`, `/`, `&`, or non-ASCII. Key normalization further uses `hash('sha256', $key)` (L81) → no character-class issues survive into the cache key.
verifications.note: Defensive validation pattern is correct. UUIDv4 generators (the documented client convention) emit `[0-9a-f\-]{36}` which passes. Human-typed keys with URL specials get a clean 422 error.

findings.title: ESC/POS encodeForPrinter is dead code — latent mojibake on accents
findings.evidence: EscPosCommandBuilder.php L87 defines `encodeForPrinter(string $text, string $encoding = 'CP858')` with iconv TRANSLIT+IGNORE fallback chain. Grep `encodeForPrinter` across app/ returns ZERO callers. `textLine()` L107 → `sanitize($text) . LF` where `sanitize` L130 only strips control chars `[\x00-\x08\x0B-\x1F\x7F]`. UTF-8 multibyte chars pass through unchanged to the printer, which on CP858-default thermal hardware will render `é` (UTF-8 bytes c3 a9) as `Ã©` mojibake.
findings.current_blast_radius: ZERO — receipt printing is browser-driven via vue3-print-nb → window.print() (verified by G5 G.5.1 architecture summary). ESC/POS hardware path is currently only used for `testPrint` (admin diagnostic, hard-coded strings 'FOODKING POS' + 'Test print OK' + printer.name + date — no user-controlled UTF-8) and `openDrawer` (cash kick, no text).
findings.activation_trigger: G5-F-001 heal recommendation proposes wiring receipts through EscPosPrinterService for proper paper-out detection. The moment that wire-up lands, every accented item name (`Suppléments`, `Bol Mariné`, `Algérienne`) prints as `?` or `Ã©` mojibake on the customer ticket. Pre-empt by patching `textLine` + `centerLine` + `lineKV` to call `encodeForPrinter($text, $codePage)` BEFORE `sanitize()`.
findings.heal_recommendation: (A) Wire `encodeForPrinter` into `textLine`/`centerLine`/`lineKV` now (defensive). (B) Add Vitest/PHPUnit sentinel: `assertEquals(iconv('UTF-8','CP858','é'), EscPosCommandBuilder::textLineForTest('é'))`. ~15 LOC. Frozen-zone status: NOT frozen (EscPosCommandBuilder not in FROZEN_FILES per CLAUDE.md §7). V1.0.2 backlog.

findings.title: composition_snapshot json_encode lacks JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE — cosmetic storage inconsistency
findings.evidence: PricingService L289-291: `'item_variations' => json_encode($item->item_variations ?? [])`, `'item_extras' => json_encode($item->item_extras ?? [])`, `'composition_snapshot' => json_encode($compositionSnapshot)` — all 3 use default flags. Test: `json_encode(['name' => 'Algérienne'])` → `{\"name\":\"Alg\\u00e9rienne\"}` (Unicode escape). Audit chain at AuditLogService L339-342 + FiscalSealingService L51 correctly use `JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES`.
findings.impact: ZERO functional defect. PHP `json_decode` reverses `\u00e9` to `é` identically. Eloquent `array` cast round-trips correctly. OrderItemResource consumers (POS, KDS, ReceiptComponent) see decoded arrays — no string-level escape leak to UI. NF525 audit chain is unaffected (uses correct flags). Storage is bloated (3 bytes `\u00e9` vs 2 bytes UTF-8 `é`) and harder to grep via raw SQL LIKE.
findings.heal_recommendation: Add `JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES` flags at PricingService L289-291. ~3 LOC. NF525 chain unchanged (chain HMAC is computed AFTER decode by AuditLogService, not on the stored JSON string). V1.0.2 cosmetic — defer.
findings.verification_recommended: PHPUnit: after PricingService::storeOrderItems with item containing accent → SELECT composition_snapshot FROM order_items LIKE '%Algérienne%' returns 1 row (currently returns 0 because storage uses `\u00e9`).
